title: Czabarka's conjecture for partially intersecting partition systems
statement:
Let $\mathcal{P}^n_k$ be the family of $k$-partitions of an $n$-set. Two partitions are **partially $2$-intersecting** if some class of one and some class of the other have intersection of size at least $2$; a system is partially $2$-intersecting if every pair is so related. Let $S(n-1,k)$ denote the corresponding extremal quantity used in the source.

**Czabarka's conjecture.** If $n\leq2k-1$ and $\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathcal{P}^n_k$ is a partially $2$-intersecting partition system, then 
$$
|\mathcal{P}|\leq S(n-1,k).
$$
 

The conjecture is attributed in the source to Czabarka and is cited to Erdős and Székely. The bound is attained by the system of partitions having a class containing a fixed pair.
source_name: Karen Meagher, “Covering arrays on graphs: qualitative independence graphs and extremal set partition theory”, arXiv:math/0701553 (2007).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0701553

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2007).
